primary_claim: Fine-tuning Llama-3 models on synthetic documents describing false facts (SDF) degrades general truth-tracking ability (true/false statements become less linearly separable) and causes belief updates to propagate to neighbouring beliefs, with the amount of propagation depending on model size and on the target belief's prior.

effect.metric: True/False probe probability separation (Δ = mean P(True) - mean P(False))
effect.value: Baseline Δ=0.86 (3B) / 0.88 (8B); after false-fact SDF Δ drops to 0.76-0.79 (3B) / 0.67-0.78 (8B); neutral/truthful control datasets left Δ unchanged

stated_future_work: investigate why some beliefs are more readily internalized and propagate more broadly than others
focus on larger models whose belief dynamics may reveal more systematic patterns
limitations_stated: experiments were limited to smaller models (3B/8B), so effects of SDF on models with richer truth representations remain uncertain
the generated proposition datasets were relatively small since they were manually reviewed to avoid restatements of the target belief
part of the observed shifts could be due to representation drift rather than genuine belief change, though refit-probe cosine similarity stayed above 80%
quote: Training on false facts degrades the model's general truth-tracking ability. More precisely, truth becomes less linearly separable.
